Coati 0.2.0-alpha reads the bundles of [MEME](https://github.com/enerplanet/meme) 0.2.0-alpha, the power flows among them. Coati is a Python package and command line tool that read the netCDF and HDF5 result files of Calliope, PyPSA and AdOpT-NET0 and write what a solved model says as JSON, in the same terms for every framework. It needs none of the frameworks, nor xarray: h5py and NumPy suffice.

It is an alpha. The layout of the documents is versioned on its own (`schema_version` 1.0, unchanged by this release) and is meant to stay; the Python interface and the command line may still change between pre-releases. If a document says something other than what a framework says about the same file, please [open an issue](https://github.com/enerplanet/Coati/issues) with the file and the two numbers.

## Highlights

- **Power flows.** A PyPSA network that `n.pf()` or `n.lpf()` solved for a dispatch that was given has no objective; Coati used to report it as not solved. Its document now carries the capacities that were given, the dispatch, the demand and the exchange as solved, and under `details.power_flow` the slack buses, the voltage of every bus, the reactive power of every generator and storage unit and the loading of every line and transformer. The convergence, which PyPSA does not record, is taken from `power_flow/convergence.csv` next to the network, as MEME writes it: `termination_condition` is `converged` or `not_converged`, and `unknown` without a record.
- **Reads the bundles of MEME 0.2.0-alpha.** Every scenario and example of MEME 0.2.0-alpha was run on every target that accepts it: 158 jobs, of which 155 ran through (three failed in the solvers of MEME) and left 197 result files, seven of them power flows. Every document agrees with what PyPSA 1.2.4, Calliope 0.7.0, Calliope 0.6.8 and AdOpT-NET0 0.1.10 themselves report for the file, and every power flow with the tables MEME writes from the solved network.
- **The names of MEME.** A bus named `north::electricity` carries `electricity` whatever its attribute `carrier` says, as the documentation promised; MEME gives every bus of an electrical network the carrier `AC`. A generator of the carrier `unmet` is demand that is not met. The page [With MEME](https://enerplanet.github.io/Coati/usage/meme/) tells how an energy-sized storage, a copperplate, a priced line, modules and investment periods of MEME appear in a document.
- **Two costs put right.** A committable unit that was never off has no series of its status in the file, since the default is on, and its stand-by cost was counted as nothing. And a technology whose output is the noise of a solver, 1e-14 either way, no longer appears in the dispatch by the sign of that noise.

## Frameworks

| Identifier | Framework | Versions | Tested with | Formats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `calliope-v0-6` | Calliope | 0.6.x | 0.6.8, 0.6.10 | netCDF-4 |
| `calliope-v0-7` | Calliope | 0.7.x | 0.7.0.dev7, 0.7.0 | netCDF-4 |
| `pypsa-v0` | PyPSA | 0.25 and later 0.x | 0.25.2, 0.35.2 | netCDF-4, HDF5 |
| `pypsa-v1` | PyPSA | 1.x | 1.2.4, 1.3.0 | netCDF-4, HDF5 |
| `adopt-net0-v0-1` | AdOpT-NET0 | 0.1.x | 0.1.10 | HDF5 |

## Getting it

```bash
pip install enerplanet-coati               # once the package is on PyPI
pip install enerplanet_coati-0.2.0a0-py3-none-any.whl   # the wheel attached below
coati files/run_0/output/network.nc results.json pypsa-v1-2-4
```

Python 3.10 or newer. The package is called `enerplanet-coati` on PyPI, the Python package and the command `coati`; `0.2.0a0` is how Python writes the version `0.2.0-alpha`.

Documentation: <https://enerplanet.github.io/Coati> (quickstart, command line, Python package, how each key follows from a file of each framework, the documents and their schemas, reading the bundles of MEME).

## What changed

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/enerplanet/Coati/blob/v0.2.0-alpha/CHANGELOG.md#020-alpha---2026-10-25).

## Known limitations

- The convergence of a power flow is known only from the record that MEME writes next to the network; without it the document says `unknown`, since PyPSA does not record it.
- The shadow prices of Calliope and PyPSA are not read, nor the inputs of a power flow: the set points, the controls and the shunt impedances.
- The costs of a PyPSA network with several investment periods are not reconciled with its objective, which weighs the periods.
- AdOpT-NET0 0.1.10 writes the node design, the operation and the energy balances of the last investment period in place of those of every period; Coati warns about such a file and cannot restore what it lacks. Its emissions are reported under `details.summary` as totals only.
- A PyPSA network that was optimised in several steps, or with an objective of its own, has an objective that is no cost; the document reports what the system costs as `objective` and what PyPSA recorded as `objective_function_value`, with a warning.
- Calliope 0.6 needs a version of Python that Coati does not support, so its files are tested from files that were made once; the other frameworks are also solved anew by the tests.
